rows.note: Use this for a very small amount, especially in cooking instructions such as adding a dash of vinegar.

example.english: Just add a dash of vinegar to the soup.
example.traditional: 湯入面加少少醋就得喇。
example.jyutping: tong1 jap6 min6 gaa1 siu2 siu2 cou3 zau6 dak1 laa3

rows.note: Use this for the punctuation mark itself; it is the standard term rather than the everyday quantity word.

example.english: This dash is used to separate the two parts of a sentence.
example.traditional: 呢個破折號係用嚟分開句子兩邊嘅。
example.jyutping: ni1 go3 po3 zit3 hou6 hai6 jung6 lei4 fan1 hoi1 geoi3 zi2 loeng5 bin1 ge3

rows.note: This is the all-purpose choice when someone runs very fast, especially toward or across somewhere.

example.english: They dash across the road whenever they see a bus.
example.traditional: 佢哋一見到巴士就衝過馬路。
example.jyutping: keoi5 dei6 jat1 gin3 dou3 baa1 si6 zau6 cung1 gwo3 maa5 lou6

rows.note: Use this colloquial verb when someone is leaving abruptly or says they have to dash.

example.english: I have something to do, so I have to dash now.
example.jyutping: ngo5 jau5 si6 jiu3 sim2 laa3

rows.traditional: 令 A 嘅希望落空
rows.jyutping: ling6 A ge3 hei1 mong6 lok6 hung1
rows.note: Use this construction when an event or person causes someone's hopes or expectations to fail.

example.english: If they cancel the travel plan, that will dash my hopes.
example.traditional: 佢哋一取消個旅行計劃，就會令我嘅希望落空。
example.jyutping: keoi5 dei6 jat1 ceoi2 siu1 go3 leoi5 hang4 gai3 waak6 zau6 wui5 ling6 ngo5 ge3 hei1 mong6 lok6 hung1

rows.note: Use this when dash means quickly jotting or writing something down, rather than merely doing something hastily.

example.english: Read me the phone number and I’ll dash it down right away.
example.traditional: 你講住個電話號碼，我即刻寫低。
example.jyutping: nei5 gong2 zyu6 go3 din6 waa2 hou6 maa5 ngo5 zik1 hak1 se2 dai1
